content:
Not wanting to miss out on this summer of AI-generated counterexamples, Alex Torzewski and I have used ChatGPT 5.6 Sol to produce examples of Tate rings that are uniform and sheafy but not stably uniform, answering Question 7 of the Nonarchimedean Scottish Book (see also Remark 2.8.11 of Kedlaya–Liu). You can find a draft write-up of the results here, which was made using @David Roe’s PaperForge.

The examples have been fully formalised in Lean (v4.33.0) and are sorry-free, building on a project of mine to formalise the basic theory of adic spaces using Claude. The results have been run through Comparator, and we have a formalization.yaml for the project. Currently, the general theory of adic spaces is also being PR’d to Tau Ceti as part of this roadmap.

Can I ask what the slides/buttons in the top-right are doing? It seems that the "detail" slider opens/closes the proof dropdown boxes, but I can't figure out what the "manual" and "?" buttons do.
That's part of paper forge, and I must admit I've not yet figured out what they do or how to disable them.

You should be able to hover over them and see what they do. The ? disables notation hovers (I'm not sure if Chris implemented any of them), and the manual button reruns the expand/contract decisions you've selected (as opposed to detail =0 or detail=1 which globally sets them). I admit they could be styled better...

The tree of definitions one needs to read for one of the results linked in the main theorem: https://remydegenne.github.io/uniform-sheafy-tate-domains-lean/chapter-fjp/module-fjp-over-strongsheafy/decl-FiniteJetOver___finiteJet_tateExt_isSheafyComplete_of_dvr/

The parts that don't depend on being "sheafy" don't depend on that many definitions. For example https://remydegenne.github.io/uniform-sheafy-tate-domains-lean/chapter-fjp/module-fjp-over-sheafyendpoints/decl-FiniteJetOver___finiteJet_isDomain/#FiniteJetOver___finiteJet_isDomain
